Q: Converting an ELF binary into an .o file A:

Actually, here is the idea I see with couple of multi-core applications. You can create a binary blob out of elf file (objcopy) and then use assembler to include that binary blob in the predetermined location. To access variables (shared, for example) from that binary blob, you should be able to create a linker file (ld) from that child elf file, which you pass to the build of the parent elf, that allows you to access variables or even functions from that binary blob.

So here is the flow:

  • build child elf

  • convert child elf to bin (objcopy)

  • create shared linker symbols map of the child elf (objdump) to create child linker file

  • include bin blob with assembly into .S file (this file has fixed name - so child bin blob should have fixed name)

  • add the assembled .S file (now .o) and child linker file into the link command of parent elf

That child elf can be for a different core, etc., but you need to keep in mind that passed flags are kindof compatible (for usage of shared linker symbols).

Q: Django using get_user_model vs settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL A:

In Django, both get_user_model() and settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL are used to reference the user model, especially when defining relationships between models. Although they serve a similar purpose, they are intended for slightly different use cases.

1. get_user_model()

get_user_model() is a helper function from django.contrib.auth that returns the user model currently configured for the project. It is typically used when you need access to the actual user model class at runtime.

This approach ensures your code continues to work even if the project switches from Django’s default user model to a custom one.

Example usage in a model:

from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.db import models

class SomeModel(models.Model):
    user = models.ForeignKey(get_user_model(), on_delete=models.CASCADE)

2. settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL

settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL is a string reference (e.g., "accounts.CustomUser") that points to the configured user model. It is commonly used in model field definitions where Django expects a model reference but importing the model directly could cause circular import issues.

This is also the recommended approach for defining relationships in reusable apps.

Example of a custom user model:

from django.contrib.auth.models import AbstractBaseUser, BaseUserManager
from django.db import models

class CustomUserManager(BaseUserManager):
    def create_user(self, email, password=None, **extra_fields):
        if not email:
            raise ValueError("The Email field must be set")
        email = self.normalize_email(email)
        user = self.model(email=email, **extra_fields)
        user.set_password(password)
        user.save(using=self._db)
        return user

class CustomUser(AbstractBaseUser):
    email = models.EmailField(unique=True)
    # ...
    objects = CustomUserManager()

Using settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL as a string reference in another model:

from django.conf import settings
from django.db import models

class Profile(models.Model):
    user = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    bio = models.TextField(blank=True)

By using a string reference, Django avoids importing the user model directly, helping prevent circular dependencies and making your app more flexible.

Q: Fixing Milvus Build Failure When make Cannot Download Third-Party Source Package on Ubuntu A:

There are different possible approaches:

- Work from a fork of conan-center-index Github repo, modify the conandata.yml file that contains the URLs of the sources to point to an alternative URL you provide. Conan admits several URLs, so it will try one after another until one works, with the condition they are exact mirrors with exactly same checksum. Then do a conan create and then conan upload to upload a copy of the package to your own private server

- You can try the "backup-sources" feature. By downloading first that binary in a computer that is not affected. Check https://blog.conan.io/2023/10/03/backup-sources-feature.html and https://docs.conan.io/2/devops/backup_sources/sources_backup.html. Any command that tries to download the source plus a conan cache backup-upload can populate the backup sources

Of course the obvious solution is configure the network/proxy to allow downloading from those URLs
